title: Test the other direction
hook: Knowing a word from its meaning does not check the reverse direction.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: Distinguish two directions of an arbitrary word-pair mapping.

objective: Distinguish two directions of an arbitrary word-pair mapping.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Knowing a word from its meaning does not check the reverse direction. Which checks meaning-to-word retrieval? Correct option: Hide the word. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred.

claims.text: Reverse the cue and answer to check the opposite mapping. A result in one direction is not a test of the other.
claims.source: Roediger & Karpicke (2006), Test-Enhanced Learning, Psychological Science 17(3),249–255, DOI10.1111/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x; publisher abstract retrieved 2026-10-13: https://www.psychologicalscience.org/journals/psychological-science/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x/ . Prose-passage experiments found delayed retention advantages for retrieval over restudy. This short exercise does not establish that effect for the learner. Fixture mappings and rules are explicit conventions, not empirical demonstrations.

claims.text: Every displayed result is computed from the visible exercise state: recall. One short reconstruction; not a retention experiment. The reveal reports this same state and never translates its score into a personal productivity or memory benefit.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts and src/components/lifehacks/StudyLesson.tsx, reverse-the-flashcard fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts. Stage rules: check reconstructed token positions against the covered target; count exact matches out of three.

claims.text: Recall question answer and rationale: Hide the word. Reverse the cue and answer to check the opposite mapping. A result in one direction is not a test of the other.
